answer: Time-locked collateral contracts curb Sybil attacks by requiring agents to escrow funds before interacting. Instead of deploying a shifting dune of cheap bots, an attacker must commit capital as the structural timber behind each identity. The verifiable cost per agent is the sacrificed liquidity incurred until identity weight reaches its zenith. A key limitation is that upfront financial deposits disproportionately marginalize honest, underfunded participants.
